teaser: sgit's encryption and open source matter less as features than as constraints: they remove the temptations that lead to server code, lock-in and bad decisions.
core_idea: Client-side encryption and open source are constraints whose main value is not the obvious one: encryption moves protection from the data to the keys and the sovereignty line to whoever holds them, without removing GDPR, but above all it removes the temptation to process on the server, so there is no server code and features like scoped clones follow; open source removes the temptations of lock-in, the evaluation edition and building every customer's integration, which is why it has to be all of it, and leaves selling customisation as the business model.

Encryption on the client moves the problem from the data to the keys, and the sovereignty line with it.
